title: Homogeneity Across Prompt Styles: Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models

original_idea.title: Homogeneity Across Prompt Styles: Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models
original_idea.problem: It is unknown whether instruction tuning is the primary driver of inter-model homogeneity or whether homogeneity exists at the base model level.
original_idea.direction: Compare inter-model similarity between base model variants vs. their instruction-tuned counterparts on a matched set of prompts from Infinity-Chat, isolating the contribution of instruction tuning to homogeneity.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Identifying instruction tuning as a driver would point directly at the intervention needed -- more diverse fine-tuning data and procedures.
original_idea.relevant_context: RLHF reduces diversity vs. SFT (ICLR 2024); Artificial Hivemind documents the endpoint but not the mechanism; this design would partially resolve the mechanism question.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: identifying instruction tuning as the driver of homogeneity directly points to the intervention needed, making this actionable research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: comparing base vs. instruction-tuned model variants requires running open-source models in both configurations, which is feasible with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: controlled comparison isolating instruction tuning's contribution to homogeneity on a matched prompt set.

novelty.reasoning: The ICLR 2024 paper directly shows RLHF reduces output diversity compared to SFT, which partially answers the mechanism question. However, no study isolates instruction tuning's specific contribution to INTER-model homogeneity (as opposed to intra-model diversity reduction). The Artificial Hivemind effect is about convergence ACROSS models, which is a different dimension than what existing RLHF diversity work measures.

evidence.source: Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity (ICLR 2024)
evidence.finding: RLHF significantly reduces output diversity compared to SFT across a variety of measures. RLHF produces less diverse text on some metrics even when sampling for different inputs.

evidence.source: The Price of Format: Diversity Collapse in LLMs (arXiv 2505.18949)
evidence.finding: Structural homogeneity (from formatting) contributes to diversity collapse beyond content-level effects.

evidence.source: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse (NeurIPS 2025)
evidence.finding: Post-training alignment causes mode collapse; typicality bias in preference data is a fundamental driver.
